name: Scratch Acid
label: Touch and Go
lede: Five years, well over a hundred shows, a singer who hid cookie dough in his pants, and a breakup that seeded the Jesus Lizard and Rapeman.

eras.title: Two-word lists and a fired singer
eras.text: Scratch Acid started in Austin as a five-piece with David Yow on bass. They wanted nothing to do with hardcore's speed rules: the members cite Public Image Ltd, Killing Joke, Chrome and Led Zeppelin. After one show the singer was gone and Yow was the frontman.

years.h: Scratch Acid forms in Austin with David Yow on bass
years.p: Steve Anderson sings, David Yow plays bass, David Wm. Sims and Brett Bradford play guitar and Rey Washam drums. Sims says they picked the name from long lists of two-word combinations.

years.h: First show at Studio 29, then singer Steve Anderson is out
years.p: Scratch Acid's first show, at Austin's Studio 29, is three instrumentals. Steve Anderson is dismissed without notice; David Wm. Sims moves to bass and David Yow becomes the singer.

years.h: Scratch Acid's real debut pays $20 at the Skyline Club
years.p: With David Yow now singing, Scratch Acid plays the Skyline Club in Austin on a bill with TSOL, [[Big Boys|fde1cff2-5a7b-4e8c-9666-110fa90500fb]] and [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]]. The band's pay: $20.
years.xp: Rey Washam left soon after to drum for [[Big Boys|fde1cff2-5a7b-4e8c-9666-110fa90500fb]], and Rich Malley filled in until Washam came back late in 1983.

eras.title: Cookie dough and a cross
eras.text: Scratch Acid became Austin's craziest live band. According to the Austin American-Statesman's oral history, David Yow played Jesus on a cross he built one weekend and Hitler the next, and once charged the crowd with cookie dough stuffed down his pants. They wrote slowly, toured little, and never saw money from their first label.

years.p: Eight songs recorded in July 1984 at Earth & Sky Studio in Austin. Wikipedia says it reached No. 26 on the UK indie chart; [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] later ranked it No. 7 in a list of favorite albums in his journal.

years.h: Scratch Acid opens for Motörhead in Dallas
years.p: Scratch Acid gets put in front of a [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] crowd in Dallas in 1985.

years.h: Just Keep Eating, Scratch Acid's only album · Rabid Cat
years.p: The title, the band said, was an inside joke about living together and scraping by. Liner notes later said they were never paid by Rabid Cat or its European distributor.

q: I'd been drinking a little too much before the show.
years.h: Rey Washam and Brett Bradford fight onstage in Minneapolis
years.p: At a 1986 Minneapolis show, drummer Rey Washam and guitarist Brett Bradford clash onstage, and Washam leaves the tour.

years.h: Europe in a diesel Mercedes van, with Simon Bonney as roadie
years.p: Scratch Acid tours Europe over the winter of 1986–87 in a diesel Mercedes van, with Crime and the City Solution's Simon Bonney as roadie. The Christmas Eve crowd: one bartender and one drunk.
years.xp: Rey Washam told the Statesman that coming from Texas, they had no idea what real cold was. Other road stories from the Austin Chronicle: stealing [[Public Image Ltd|68950696-ee9a-49b2-a8c2-d1d6c19355cc]]'s food and drink after John Lydon refused Yow a beer, and [[Joey Ramone|2f3f8fb1-e5dc-4548-9601-fada0485e561]] telling Yow nice show.

eras.title: Berserker, and a thousand dollars
eras.text: Scratch Acid made one record for Touch and Go and quit without announcing it. Within a year three of them were in Chicago, splitting into Rapeman and The Jesus Lizard.

years.h: Berserker EP, Scratch Acid's Touch and Go debut
years.p: Scratch Acid's last record, and its first for Touch and Go. According to Wikipedia it reached No. 7 on the UK indie chart.
play: Mary Had a Little Drug Problem

q: That last show we made like $1,000.
years.h: Scratch Acid's last show, at Austin's Cave Club
years.p: No farewell announcement: Scratch Acid just plays the Cave Club and stops. Rey Washam remembers it as the best payday they ever had.

years.h: Rapeman and the Jesus Lizard come out of Scratch Acid
years.p: David Wm. Sims and Rey Washam join [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] in [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]]; Sims and David Yow move to Chicago and start [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] with [[Duane Denison|6a22c1ff-42c8-4c53-afa8-58f4766b9096]].

eras.title: The Greatest Gift
eras.text: Touch and Go gathered everything onto one disc, and the members went on to Ministry, the Melvins, accounting and acting. Twenty years after the last show, the original four came back for Touch and Go's birthday.

years.h: The Greatest Gift collects all of Scratch Acid
years.p: Touch and Go's compilation puts the EP, Just Keep Eating and Berserker on one release.
years.xp: Rey Washam went on to drum for [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]], [[Helios Creed|26a13357-fad6-4900-a324-ff252e681112]], [[The Didjits|e3d01dcb-eb41-4ce9-8506-bfd70aa8d651]], [[Lard|4430600b-0fdb-43a1-be52-c81aa7ab1682]] and [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]], and sometimes the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]]. Brett Bradford stayed in Austin and played in Great Caesar's Ghost, Sangre de Toro, Areola 51 and later Suckling.

years.h: The original four reunite at Emo's in Austin
years.p: After four days of six- to eight-hour practices, Scratch Acid plays Emo's on September 2, Touch and Go's 25th anniversary in Chicago on September 9, and Seattle's Showbox on September 16.
years.xp: Washam told the Statesman it was strange counting off the first song after so many years away.

years.h: Scratch Acid's first US tour in 24 years
years.p: Scratch Acid announces US dates for November and December 2011.

years.h: First UK show since 1987, at Jeff Mangum's ATP
years.p: Scratch Acid plays All Tomorrow's Parties, curated by [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]]: its first UK show since the 1986–87 tour.

sources.title: Austin American-Statesman: An oral history, from Scratch
